derivedFrom: software/_connector/versions/1.0.4 (its four text files, byte for byte)
releaseScope: Architecture 3.2, step P7 (qoder binding): a re-seal, not a behaviour change. 1.0.4 was published with a SHA256SUMS row naming __pycache__/connector.cpython-39.pyc, which git never tracked - so any platform checking this repository out gets "listed-file-missing" against the release it is told to run, and the shared repository carries a compiled binary, which BP-1 forbids (the repos hold freezable text). This release seals the files that are actually versioned.
changes: SHA256SUMS: regenerated over the four versioned text files; no __pycache__ row
unchanged: connector.py, README.md, schemas/software-admin-v1.schema.json - digests verified equal to 1.0.4 before this release was written
the Burp native MCP SSE path added in 1.0.4, and every earlier surface: the engine-facing shapes, session lifecycle, credential materialization and the refusal-redaction rules
1.0.0 through 1.0.4 remain published and immutable, including 1.0.4 with its bad seal

knownDefectThisFixes.shape: a published release whose own hash manifest lists an untracked file
knownDefectThisFixes.howItWasFound: the P3 battery seal cell went red while smoke-testing the production binding, after a stray __pycache__ directory was removed from the working tree
knownDefectThisFixes.operationalNote: the removal was done before checking git, and the file was untracked - so the one on-disk copy of a sealed digest is gone and 1.0.4 can no longer be re-verified against it. The functional bytes were never at risk (the four text files still match their digests), and the recorded lesson is: inspect and copy a sealed release before deleting anything inside it
knownDefectThisFixes.guard: the seal check now also asserts every listed row is tracked by git, so the class is machine-caught instead of rediscovered by an editor

pointerPolicy: software/_connector/current.json moves 1.0.4 -> 1.0.5. This is the same registered discipline as the earlier self-moves of this resource (§8.25 deviation 3), and qoder production now resolves its softwareGateway through this pointer.

selftest.seal: every row of SHA256SUMS exists on disk, matches its digest, and is tracked by git
selftest.batteries: P3 98 cells, P4a 41 cells, P5 35 cells rerun against the pinned release
